title: One-hop import trap: api imports runtime_state and schema; contextvars TODO is scope bait
description: Type E (hidden dependency + scope bait). The api.py imports both runtime_state.py and schema.py — these are real one-hop dependencies the decomposer must declare in context closure. The runtime_state module has a non-blocking TODO(contextvars) that tempts scope expansion; a good plan names it as an out-of-scope non-goal with the exact TODO reference. store.py is a frozen module the task must not own. Good plans: declare all three imports in the API task's required_context, name the contextvars TODO as a non-goal, exclude store.py from owned paths, and keep the batch endpoint and schema in one leaf. Anti-plans: miss the runtime_state import (hidden dependency — it's not the API itself but a one-hop dependency the executor discovers mid-task); expand scope to fix the contextvars TODO; claim ownership of store.py ('while I'm at it'); or split the endpoint and schema into two tasks when one closure suffices.
